If my username isn't enough, let me introduce myself. I am ShitladyOfTheSkies, and I work at a medium-sized airport in the US as ground operations for a major airline.When I first started at the airport a couple of years ago I was a tubster, teetering around a 26-27 BMI. I had just left my job in finance because it was slowly choking the life out of me, and I stumbled into what has become my dream job here at the airport. In the first 3 months I dropped 30lbs (13.5ish kg) thanks to all the walking (and sometimes panicked running) I do in a day. Around this time I became acquainted with /r/fatlogic, which became my gateway drug. Despite my newfound awareness and steadily growing intolerance for fatlogic bullshit, I still shied away from FPH, thinking it too extreme. That is, until The Incident.

The Incident occurred right around this season a few years ago. Just as Christmas travel was picking up, and weather was getting bad. Every flight was oversold, under even more strain as we tried to find flights for the many passengers who had been delayed or cancelled by shitty weather. Cut to our DEN flight, blessedly the last flight of the day, delayed a solid 3 hours. I had handled it almost entirely by myself up at the gate, rebooking about seventy passengers and retagging dozens and dozens of bags.

During this time, one passenger kept pestering me. We'll call her Tabitha Tatertwat, first because she couldn't seem to stop mashing potatoes- of all various forms- into her face, and second because she just looked like a goddamn potato. She could've been a dead ringer for Simply Sara, if Sara had lost all of her front teeth and half her hair.

Ms. Tatertwat was not content with any of the accommodations we provided her for her delay. While I was rebooking her, she kept snorting rude remarks under her breath over and over for me to hear, like "Fucking bullshit" or "Stupid fucking assholes" as if the weather were our fault. She was angry about the airport wheelchair she had been provided, complaining it was too small, and demanding that I step away every 30 minutes to roll her to the bathroom less than 20 yards from the gate. Her inability to roll herself to the bathroom certainly didn't stop her from wheeling over and wedging herself between my counter and the line of other passengers every once in awhile to complain. Or to demand that we "Get a new plane already", even after I had politely explained at least 5 times that I am simply not capable of pulling a 737-700 out of my ass. When we began passing out food vouchers, she was furious that a family of 5 got a total of $70 while she got only $14, at which point I could barely keep myself from tearing her piggy little head off her greasy shoulders. I stopped acknowledging her entirely at this point, my nerves frayed.

The whole day leading up to this, I had been hellbent on finding a flight for a 7 year old girl and her grandmother flying to see her mother. For 2 days every single time she had been rebooked the flight would be cancelled, or delayed so badly she would miss her connection. Finally, this last flight was looking promising. I had even convinced several people to fly the next day so that there would be 2 open seats, just for them.

At last, the plane taking them to DEN was on the ground and we were boarding. Tatertwat was on board and out of my hair, and I was cracking jokes over the intercom to keep the restless passengers smiling. Just as the little girl and her grandmother were boarding, the line up the jetbridge slowed to a complete halt. A panicked looking flight attendant came trotting up to the boarding podium, and breathlessly informed me there were not enough seats. I started frantically going through paperwork, looking for what I could have possibly missed, where we were miscounting.

Then I realized with horror: Tabby Tatertwat was not designated an Extra Seat. She certainly wasn't self-aware to book one for herself, and I hadn't thought about it enough to book the seat for her. There was only 1 spot left on the plane, and since the little girl would have to connect in DEN, she couldn't make the trip alone. I would have to see if Tabby could be persuaded to give up her seats, and fly the next day.

Mortified, I trudged down to the aircraft. I spotted Tabby in her seat(s) and crouched down to ask her- no, beg her- to please consider flying out on our very first flight tomorrow, so that the little girl and her grandmother could see their family. I offered her hundreds in vouchers, a hotel, all the food vouchers she could want, anything, if she would please just delay her trip just one day. I'll never forget what she said to me:

"You're lucky I don't spit in your face! That's not MY PROBLEM. I'm going HOME!"

I flinched as she shrieked the word "home". With angry tears in my eyes, I turned and walked off the plane, shaking with rage. At the top of the jetbridge the girl and her grandmother saw my crestfallen face, and started crying too.

Eventually, I found the little girl a flight to see her mother. I still see her every once in awhile, actually, and she's an adorable kid. We always high five, and I let her tell jokes on the intercom, or sing songs from Frozen to the passengers.

I've also seen Tabby Tatertwat. She's as fat and mean as ever, hasn't changed a bit.

But one thing has changed. Now, I don't shy away from my hatred. Now, I'm a militant Shitlady, proud member of FPH. Since that day, and for every day until I die, I've made it my mission to make flying pigs cry.

That premise not quite accurate. First of all, there may be different types of natural selection forces acting - group selection, sexual selection, and yes, individual genetic selection. The output will be some combination of those forces. Also, I would argue that individual selection is most interested in furthering one's genes than survival of oneself. That is, reproduction/furthering of one's genes is a the ultimate goal, not necessarily a long life.

For example, if a man is uncertain that a child in his pair bond is his own biologically, he is more likely to leave his inheritance to his sister's offspring because there is where his genes are more likely to benefit from his resources (avuncular inheritance). Also, in bee colonies, if there is some threat to the hive, the bees will not save the offspring - they will save their siblings, because by some fancy genetic mechanism, they share more genes with their siblings than the offspring (kin selection).

Anyways... To get to your point - I suppose greed is the common thread that allows for the survival of our genes. But I do not think we are getting greedier. We are shifting towards a more uniform division of resources. Our frontal cortices (centers of reasoning) are tamping down on our more primal brain areas that would only favor reproduction. It may be a while before the inertia of past greed is overcome, but I think we can change things because I have faith in brain plasticity and our ability to be dynamic (unless there is just too much inertia to truly reverse things...that is another matter though). Also, having a group selection force will pull things in favor of the group instead of the individual.

With fourteen of the fifteen warmest years on record having occurred since the year 2000; with oceans both warming and acidifying; and with unequivocal scientific evidence that burning fossil fuels is the principal cause – what can we do to rapidly reduce emissions?

Similarly, the eloquent rhetoric of green growth continues to eclipse quantitative analysis demonstrating the need for radical social as well as technical change.

Taking these issues head on, this seminar will develop a quantitative framing of mitigation, based on IPCC carbon budgets, before finishing with more qualitative examples of what a genuine 2°C mitigation agenda may contain.

Kevin Anderson is professor of energy and climate change in the School of Mechanical, Aeronautical and Civil Engineering at the University of Manchester. Anderson recently finished a two-year position as director of the Tyndall Centre, the UK's leading academic climate change research organisation. Kevin’s work makes clear that there is now little to no chance of maintaining the rise in global mean surface temperature at below 2°C, despite repeated high-level statements to the contrary. Sesame Scores are indications of the users’ creditworthiness, which range from 350 to 950 points. Users will be able to check their Sesame Scores both in the Alipay Wallet mobile app and through merchant websites that accept Sesame Credit services.   • Fulfillment Capacity shows a user’s ability to fulfill his/her contract obligations. Indicators include use of financial products and services and Alipay account balances.
